title: Onboard orionx-slim-9b v1.0: metadata, perf profiles, and changelog automation
author: Sofia Mendes
description: Onboard `orionx-slim-9b` v1.0 into the model registry. This PR adds canonical metadata, recommended inference configurations, per-hardware performance profiles, and wires the model into our changelog/release-notes automation so customers see the new model in the release feed. Motivation: orionx-slim-9b is an efficient 9B variant that provides ~25% lower latency vs the baseline while keeping comparable quality on our evals. Onboarding includes: metadata.yaml with model attributes, quantization/packing recommendations, perf profiles for common sequence lengths and batch sizes, a perf test for CI, documentation and quickstart example, and an update to the changelog generator to pick up model metadata automatically. Checklist: - [x] Add model metadata and canonical identifiers (model_id, family, architecture) - [x] Add performance profiles for p3/rtx/aurora instance types - [x] Add inference knobs (max_tokens, kv_cache_hint, batch_size suggestions) - [x] Add CI perf test and unit tests - [x] Wire model into changelog/release-notes automation - [x] Update docs and quickstart snippet - [x] Smoke test on Dedicated cluster (confirmed) Related: Linear ENG-4123 (onboarding), ENG-4198 (perf validation). See internal perf run link: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/2026-02-07/orionx-slim-9b. Notes: - We include an initial int8 quantization profile and a conservative int4 suggestion (opt-in) — int4 remains experimental. - Perf numbers were collected with batching disabled for latency SLOs and with continuous batching for throughput profiles to produce both latency/throughput recommendations. Rollout plan: merge to main, CI will run perf smoke and unit tests; enable model in staging registry tier for 24h; if metrics stable, rollout to hosted catalog. Release notes automation: updated scripts will generate an entry under "Model registry updates" with summary and link to perf profiles. If rollback needed revert this PR and remove model entry from registry index.
